# .github/workflows/docs-requirements.txt
#
# HASH-LOCKED Python dependency set for the `docs` job of
# `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the MkDocs / TechDocs site build). This file is
# the Python-side counterpart of `Cargo.lock`: it pins the COMPLETE transitive
# closure - not just the three direct requirements - to an exact version AND an
# exact artifact digest, and the workflow installs it with `--require-hashes`.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#
# The docs job previously ran, in effect,
#
#     python -m pip install 'mkdocs==1.6.1' 'mkdocs-techdocs-core==1.7.0' \
#                           'mkdocs-mermaid2-plugin==1.2.3'
#
# which pins three names and floats the other forty-three. Those forty-three
# packages execute on the runner with full read access to the checkout, so a new
# compatible release of any one of them - or a compromised maintainer account -
# changes what CI runs with no diff in this repository and no review. Pinning the
# version alone is not enough either: `==` binds a name to a release, and a
# digest binds it to the exact bytes. `--require-hashes` is what makes the
# binding enforceable, and it additionally forbids an unpinned requirement from
# entering the resolution at all, so a dependency that appears later cannot slip
# in unnoticed - the install fails loudly instead.
#
# This is the same posture the Rust side already takes: `Cargo.lock` is committed
# and every cargo invocation in CI carries `--locked`. See AAP section 0.7.2
# standard S6 (supply-chain hygiene with concrete pinned versions) and standard
# S7 (reproducible toolchain).
#
# TARGET ENVIRONMENT
#
# CPython 3.12 on 64-bit Linux (`ubuntu-latest`), which is why the workflow pins
# `python-version` to a FULL patch release rather than the `3.12` series. Each
# entry below carries the digests of every artifact CPython 3.12 on
# manylinux-x86_64 can legitimately select: the pure-Python `py3`/`py2.py3`
# wheel, and additionally the `cp312-cp312` manylinux x86_64 wheel where the
# project publishes compiled artifacts. Source distributions are deliberately
# NOT listed and the workflow passes `--only-binary=:all:`, because building an
# sdist under `--require-hashes` would need unhashed build-time dependencies.
#
# A different interpreter minor version or a non-x86_64 runner will fail this
# install rather than silently install something else. That is the intended
# behaviour: regenerate the lock for the new target instead of relaxing the gate.
#
# HOW TO REGENERATE (do this, do not hand-edit a digest)
#
#   1. Resolve the closure for the target environment:
#
#      python -m pip download -d /tmp/docs-wheels --only-binary=:all: \
#        --python-version 3.12 --implementation cp --abi cp312 \
#        --platform manylinux_2_17_x86_64 --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 \
#        --platform manylinux_2_28_x86_64 --platform any \
#        'mkdocs==1.6.1' 'mkdocs-techdocs-core==1.7.0' \
#        'mkdocs-mermaid2-plugin==1.2.3'
#
#   2. Take each resolved name/version pair and record the sha256 digests PyPI
#      publishes for its CPython-3.12-compatible wheels (`pip hash <file>` also
#      works on the downloaded artifacts).
#   3. Verify before committing, which must exit 0:
#
#      python -m pip download -d /tmp/docs-verify --require-hashes \
#        --only-binary=:all: --python-version 3.12 --implementation cp \
#        --abi cp312 --platform manylinux_2_17_x86_64 \
#        --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 --platform manylinux_2_28_x86_64 \
#        --platform any -r .github/workflows/docs-requirements.txt
#
#   4. Bump the three direct versions ONLY in a deliberate commit, and keep the
#      assertion in the workflow's install step in step with them.
#
# THE THREE DIRECT REQUIREMENTS ARE `mkdocs`, `mkdocs-techdocs-core` and
# `mkdocs-mermaid2-plugin`; everything else below is transitive. The comment
# above each entry names the artifacts its digests cover.
# babel-2.18.0-py3-none-any.whl
